Let G G be a locally compact group with the group algebra L 1 ​ ( G ) L^{1}(G) and N N be a closed normal subgroup of G G . Suppose that ξ : N → 𝕋 \xi:N\to\mathbb{T} is a continuous character and L ξ 1 ​ ( G , N ) L_{\xi}^{1}(G,N) is the L 1 L^{1} -space of all covariant functions of ξ \xi on G G .

arxiv-2204-13711.title: Radio sky reveals primordial electron-proton interactions
arxiv-2204-13711.creator: Shyam Balaji, 1 Maura E. Ramírez-Quezada, 2 Céline Bœhm 3
arxiv-2204-13711.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shyam Balaji, 1 Maura E. Ramírez-Quezada, 2 Céline Bœhm 3. For several decades, astronomers have measured the electromagnetic emission in the universe from the lowest to the highest energies with incredible precision. The lowest end of the spectrum, corresponding to radio waves, is fairly well studied and understood. Yet there is a long standing discrepancy between measurements and predictions, which has prompted the construction of many new models of radio emitters.

arxiv-2208-06960.title: X ⁡ ( 3872 ) X(3872) and T c ​ c T_{cc} : structures and productions in heavy ion collisions
arxiv-2208-06960.creator: Hyeongock Yun, Daeho Park, Sungsik Noh, Aaron Park, Woosung Park, Sungtae Cho, Juhee Hong, Yongsun Kim, Sanghoon Lim, Su Houng Lee
arxiv-2208-06960.description: Abstract We argue why the recently observed T c ​ c T_{cc} could either be a compact multiquark configuration or a loosely bound molecular configuration composed of charmed mesons, whereas the X ⁡ ( 3872 ) X(3872) is most likely a molecular configuration.

arxiv-2301-10369.title: Exact Fractional Inference via Re-Parametrization & Interpolation between Tree-Re-Weighted- and Belief Propagation- Algorithms
arxiv-2301-10369.creator: Hamidreza Behjoo hamidreza.behjoo@gmail.com
arxiv-2301-10369.description: Abstract Computing the partition function, Z Z , of an Ising model over a graph of N N “spins” is most likely exponential in N N . Efficient variational methods, such as Belief Propagation (BP) and Tree Re-Weighted (TRW) algorithms, compute Z Z approximately by minimizing the respective (BP- or TRW-) free energy.

arxiv-2306-15923.title: A Fuzzy Classification Framework to Identify Equivalent Atoms in Complex Materials and Molecules
arxiv-2306-15923.creator: King Chun Lai, Sebastian Matera, Christoph Scheurer, Karsten Reuter
arxiv-2306-15923.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by King Chun Lai, Sebastian Matera, Christoph Scheurer, Karsten Reuter. The nature of an atom in a bonded structure – such as in molecules, in nanoparticles or solids, at surfaces or interfaces – depends on its local atomic environment. In atomic-scale modeling and simulation, identifying groups of atoms with equivalent environments is a frequent task, to gain an understanding of the material function, to interpret experimental results or to simply restrict demanding first-principles calculations.

arxiv-2402-18901.title: Electromagnetic properties of Ω c 0 \Omega_{c}^{0} resonances via light-cone QCD
arxiv-2402-18901.creator: Ulaş Özdem
arxiv-2402-18901.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ulaş Özdem. We systematically study the electromagnetic properties of controversial states whose internal structure is not elucidated and we try to offer a different point of view to unravel the internal structure of these states.

arxiv-2409-04257.title: Privacy risk from synthetic data: practical proposals
arxiv-2409-04257.creator: Gillian M Raab
arxiv-2409-04257.description: Abstract This paper proposes and compares measures of identity and attribute disclosure risk for synthetic data. Data custodians can use the methods proposed here to inform the decision as to whether to release synthetic versions of confidential data. Different measures are evaluated on two data sets.

arxiv-2412-14234.title: Syzygy : Dual Code-Test C to (safe) Rust Translation using LLMs and Dynamic Analysis
arxiv-2412-14234.creator: Manish Shetty, Naman Jain, Adwait Godbole, Sanjit A. Seshia, Koushik Sen
arxiv-2412-14234.description: Abstract . Despite extensive usage in high-performance, low-level systems programming applications, C is susceptible to vulnerabilities due to manual memory management and unsafe pointer operations. Rust, a modern systems programming language, offers a compelling alternative. Its unique ownership model and type system ensure memory safety without sacrificing performance.

arxiv-2510-16590.title: Atom-anchored LLMs speak Chemistry: A Retrosynthesis Demonstration
arxiv-2510-16590.creator: Alan Kai Hassen, Andrius Bernatavicius, Antonius P. A. Janssen, Mike Preuss, Gerard J. P. van Westen, Djork-Arné Clevert
arxiv-2510-16590.description: Abstract Applications of machine learning in chemistry are often limited by the scarcity and expense of labeled data, restricting traditional supervised methods. In this work, we introduce a framework for molecular reasoning using general-purpose Large Language Models (LLMs) that operates without requiring labeled training data. Our method anchors chain-of-thought reasoning to the molecular structure by using unique atomic identifiers.

arxiv-2601-12458.title: Symmetric Preparation of Systems
arxiv-2601-12458.creator: Nils Dencker Lund University
arxiv-2601-12458.description: Abstract . In this paper we generalize the Weierstrass and Malgrange preparation theorems to the symmetric matrix valued case, proving symmetric preparation of analytic and smooth symmetric systems that vanishes of first order. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 32B05 Secondary 47A56, 26B40 1.

arxiv-2602-09725.title: Efficient Remote Prefix Fetching with GPU-native Media ASICs
arxiv-2602-09725.creator: Liang Mi 1 Weijun Wang 2 Jinghan Chen 1 Ting Cao 2 Haipeng Dai 1 Yunxin Liu 2 1 Nanjing University 2 Institute for AI Industry Research (AIR), Tsinghua University
arxiv-2602-09725.description: Abstract . Remote KV cache reuse fetches KV cache for identical contexts from remote storage, avoiding recomputation, accelerating LLM inference. While it excels in high-speed networks, its performance degrades significantly in bandwidth-limited scenarios. Recent studies address this by transmitting KV caches in compressed form, but the associated heavyweight decompression counteracts the KV reuse benefits.

pmc-11286749.title: Liver biochemical indexes and cholesterol metabolism in cystic fibrosis patients with F508del/CFTR variant genotype after elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor treatment
pmc-11286749.creator: Alice Castaldo, Paola Iacotucci, Sveva Bagnasco, Cristina Fevola, Vincenzo Carnovale, Fabio Antonelli, Gustavo Cernera, Monica Gelzo, Vito Terlizzi
pmc-11286749.description: Modulators of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) improved cystic fibrosis (CF) patients’ outcome. The elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) combination was safe and effective improving lung function in patients with different CFTR genotypes, including at least one F508del mutation. However, cases with liver damage were reported.

pmc-11679567.title: MFF-Net: A Lightweight Multi-Frequency Network for Measuring Heart Rhythm from Facial Videos
pmc-11679567.creator: Wenqin Yan, Jialiang Zhuang, Yuheng Chen, Yun Zhang, Xiujuan Zheng, Patrick Boissy
pmc-11679567.description: Remote photo-plethysmography (rPPG) is a useful camera-based health motioning method that can measure the heart rhythm from facial videos. Many well-established deep learning models can provide highly accurate and robust results in measuring heart rate (HR) and heart rate variability (HRV).

pmc-11743468.title: Desmoid Fibromatosis Involving the Retropharyngeal and Danger Spaces: A Case Report
pmc-11743468.creator: Masami Ito, Kota Yokoyama, Yosuke Ariizumi, Yoshihito Kano, Kurara Yamamoto, Takahiro Asakage, Ukihide Tateishi
pmc-11743468.description: Desmoid fibromatosis (DF) is a rare, non-metastasizing but locally aggressive mesenchymal tumor arising from fibroblasts or myofibroblasts. We report a solitary case of DF involving the retropharyngeal and danger spaces, a location rarely documented. The patient, a woman in her 70s, presented with progressive pharyngeal discomfort over six months.

pmc-12429318.title: The Popliteofibular Ligament: A Narrative Review of Anatomical Variants and Their Surgical Relevance in Posterolateral Knee Reconstruction
pmc-12429318.creator: Łukasz Olewnik, Ingrid C. Landfald, Bartosz Gonera, Kacper Ruzik, Robert F. LaPrade
pmc-12429318.description: Purpose: This review aims to synthesize current knowledge of anatomical variations of the popliteofibular ligament (PFL) and evaluate the clinical relevance of the classification system proposed by Olewnik et al. in the context of the diagnosis, surgical treatment, and rehabilitation of posterolateral corner (PLC) injuries. Methods: A comprehensive analysis of anatomical, surgical, and radiological studies concerning the PFL was conducted.

pmc-12448166.title: Efficacy and safety of oral spironolactone for female pattern hair loss in premenopausal women: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group pilot study
pmc-12448166.creator: Pimpakarn Werachattawatchai, Saranya Khunkhet, Sarawin Harnchoowong, Chotinij Lertphanichkul
pmc-12448166.description: Background:Oral spironolactone is widely used as an alternative treatment for female pattern hair loss, particularly in women of reproductive age. However, published data on its effects are still limited.Objective:This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of spironolactone 100 mg daily for female pattern hair loss in premenopausal women compared with placebo.

pmc-12580428.title: Developing an AI framework for learning in higher education: a humanities perspective from English Literature
pmc-12580428.creator: Bridgette Wessels
pmc-12580428.description: Little is known about how to develop frameworks for using AI to support learning in English Literature within higher education. This paper presents research that developed a framework for employing AI in the study of the fourteenth-century English poet Geoffrey Chaucer.

pmc-12617951.title: Synergistic enhancement of AAV gene delivery in 2D cells and 3D organoids using polybrene and hydroxychloroquine
pmc-12617951.creator: Hyeon-Jin Na, Yongbo Shin, Seung-Hyun Kim, Seung Pil Jang, Myung Jin Son, Yong Min Choi, Hyeon Gyeol Jeon, Ok-Seon Kwon, Kyung-Sook Chung, Xiaoping Bao, Xiaoping Bao, Xiaoping Bao
pmc-12617951.description: Recent advances in three-dimensional (3D) culture platforms have enabled organoids to serve as physiologically relevant models for recapitulating human biology and assessing therapeutic efficacy and toxicity. Despite their promise, their complex architecture presents significant challenges for efficient gene delivery, thereby limiting their broader application in drug discovery and translational research.

pmc-13198262.title: Transcriptome-guided development of a fibrosis-reversal compound reduces skin scarring and allows regeneration via mitochondrial uncoupling
pmc-13198262.creator: Chun-Ye Chen, Ruilin Xu, Mingguang Mo, Jiahao Wu, Jun Chi, Zhang-Rui Wu, Yi Wang, Xin-Cao Zhong, Xiao-Ying Lin, Yang Liu, Jingdong Wu, Huaan Fang, Hongli Jia, Hongsen Bi, Yong Yang, Wei-Qiang Tan, Yang Zhao
pmc-13198262.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummarySkin scarring impairs function and aesthetics. Current therapies show limited efficacy and cause iatrogenic dermal disruption (e.g., triamcinolone acetonide [TA], a first-line corticosteroid for keloids), with topical medications demonstrating inferior outcomes. Through transcriptome-guided evaluation, we develop FR-1 (fibrosis-reversal compound 1), a small molecule that reverses fibrosis in vitro by inhibiting fibroblast proliferation, suppressing α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), and remodeling the extracellular matrix (ECM) via collagen downregulation and matrix metalloproteinase-1 (MMP1) induction.

pmc-13626491.title: Positive predictive value of tactile tracheal tube cuff ballotability above the suprasternal notch in detecting the correct positioning of the tracheal tube – A diagnostic accuracy study
pmc-13626491.creator: Viswanath Selvam, Venkata Ganesh, Sameer Vyas, Lakshmi Narayana Yaddanapudi, Hemant Bhagat
pmc-13626491.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and Aims:Most endotracheal tube (ETT) depth assessment methods require extra equipment or expertise. Suprasternal tactile cuff ballotability is a bedside technique; however, its performance against a radiographic standard is not well characterised. This study assessed the accuracy of identifying an ETT cuff position above the lower border of the second thoracic vertebral body (T2LB) on fluoroscopy, interobserver agreement, and the relationship with tip-to-carina distance.Methods:This prospective observational study enroled adults undergoing neuroradiological procedures under general anaesthesia.
